text:
Brock Faber settled back into the Wild lineup on November 14 and immediately went back to doing what Minnesota needs: playing huge minutes. He has averaged 25.9 a night in six games, with two games over 29. He has two goals and an assist, and The Athletic's Michael Russo framed the return with the headline "Brock Faber's high standards haven't budged as he settles back into Wild lineup."

The goals are a bonus, not a trend. He has scored twice on 0.62 expected goals, our measure of chance quality, and he is shooting 18.2% against a usual defenseman's 6.4%. At five on five the Wild have had 46% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about seven points worse than without him, which is worth watching for a player whose calling card is driving play: Evolving-Hockey had him at 2.3 wins above replacement last season, 23rd of 215 defensemen, with his team creating 0.16 more expected goals per 60 when he was out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags a habit: lots of shots, fewer from the slot. Our numbers project 39 points.
headline: Faber is back and playing 26 minutes again
